newsitem.title: GERMANY: German smokers in danger from fresh air lobby.
newsitem.headline: German smokers in danger from fresh air lobby.

text.p: German smokers may soon be hounded out of public offices and restaurants like their cousins in the United States after a cross-party parliamentary alliance put forward a bill on Wednesday to curtail smokers' rights.

There are few restrictions in Germany, where non-smoking sections in restaurants are rare and smoking in offices is widespread. But the sight of smokers puffing on the pavement outside office blocks may soon become commonplace.

A group of 136 politicians from the ruling centre-right coalition and opposition Social Democratic Party (SPD) proposed the bill to ban smoking in public buildings, work places and on public transport.
Offenders would be subject to a fine of up to 100 marks.
The bill followed one day after the environmentalist Greens proposed a similar motion in the Bonn federal parliament.

The German Cigarette Industry Association said: "Such a law is socially unacceptable...German people are adult enough to solve social conflict among themselves, without legal bans. They do not want a smoke police force."
Uta Tietze-Stecher, proposing the bill for the SPD, quoted the German hotel and pub association as saying its members favoured offering "attractive smoke-free zones" to customers.
The bill has drawn support from parliamentarians from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats as well as the liberal Free Democrats.

On Tuesday the Greens proposed their own bill to protect non-smokers, demanding a general ban in most public areas and pubs. The Greens also demanded a ban on cigarette vending machines, now positioned on virtually every street corner, to reduce the risk of children becoming addicted.
